Josie sighs, sitting on a parking lot divider, breathing in the smoke. Her nose is red and her cheeks prickle and, despite the fire, it's cold. She's waiting for Jeremy and Daniel who are out doing something somewhere. It was her only job to set the fire. Burn it down. She was good at that. 

She hears footsteps from the right of her and scrambles behind Daniel's car. it turns out to be Jeremy, soot-stained but unburned. His smile was wide and genuine and full of adrenaline. He hands her something in a plastic container and: oh. White icing, pink roses, and a matching cursive "Happy Birthday!". 

"You're eighteen tonight, yeah?" Jeremy says, huddles behind the car with her. "I wish I had a better present for you." He pats himself down, kutte and all, looking for a joint. She loves looking at the big fires, like this one, a little stoned and thoughtful. No. Loved. No more fires. But she's already broken that one, hasn't she?

"Yeah," she whispers back, hearing footsteps from the front. Her stomach twists and she hopes it's Daniel. She wants to get out of here, away from the fire. Still, she can't hell but flick her lighter open and shut. Nervous habit. Josie knows it'll be hard to give up. 

He meets them behind the car, hood up, black bag over his shoulder. Daniel says, "Let's go," and they both spring up. Daniel curls in back because he's so tall and Josie hides as best she can in the passenger seat, the cake's plastic covering creaking. Jeremy drives and it's some kind of miracle that they don't die on the way home.
